lf-swipe-deck.description: One rapid pass-or-keep classification Ask. Put it inside lf-ask, whose heading becomes the deck's accessible name. Cards begin in the `unseen` pile; the user sends each active card to the `pass` or `keep` pile with the labeled buttons, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, or a horizontal pointer swipe. A classified card's Return to queue button withdraws that classification, including after completion, when returning any card reopens the Ask. Each classification reaches the agent as an absolute `swipe` action, and the Ask is answered once `unseen` is empty, so the swipe that empties it answers. Children are exactly one lf-swipe-pile for each verdict. Re-emit the authored starting order unchanged on later versions: recorded classifications carry forward by card id. A rewrite that invalidates a classification takes `restated` on that card, and one that invalidates the completed deck takes it on the deck (see `$restated` in `registry.json`).

lf-swipe-pile.description: One semantic pile in a swipe deck. Supply exactly one pile for each `verdict`: `unseen` is the ordered queue, `pass` is out of scope, and `keep` is retained for follow-up. Children are lf-swipe-card elements only; cards are reparented here as recorded position state, so the verdict attribute is the classification and no card-level status is needed.

lf-swipe-card.description: One concise technical proposal in a swipe deck. Lead with a <strong> title and follow with enough prose to classify it without leaving the deck. Its id identifies it in classification details and preserves its verdict across page versions. Rewriting a classified proposal needs `restated` on this card (see lf-swipe-deck).
